tex_content.html:
↗ thm:deep-delta-necks-in-horn

The function $h(\rho ,\delta )$ may be chosen with $h\le \delta \rho $, weakly non-decreasing in $\delta $ for fixed $\rho $, and weakly non-decreasing in $\rho $ for fixed $\delta $.
Proof

↗ thm:deep-delta-necks-in-horn\sketch If $h$ works for $(\rho ,\delta )$, it works for larger parameters and every smaller positive value. Choose decreasing sequences $\rho _n,\delta _n\to 0$ and decreasing $h_n\le \rho _n\delta _n$, then define $h(\rho ,\delta )$ by the largest index with $\rho \ge \rho _n$ and $\delta \ge \delta _n$.
